0.long_answer: Hereditary angioedema is a condition characterized by improper regulation of the kallikrein-kinin system due to a deficiency or dysfunction of the C1-esterase inhibitor. This leads to increased production of bradykinin, a potent vasoactive peptide responsible for vasodilation and increased vascular permeability, resulting in the characteristic swelling seen in attacks. Bradykinin is normally degraded by angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE). When ACE activity is reduced, as in the case of ACE inhibitor use or hereditary angioedema, bradykinin levels accumulate, further contributing to angioedema.
